question: What will be the monthly change in US nonfarm payrolls (BLS) for September 2026, as first published?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the first published value of the monthly change in US nonfarm payrolls (BLS) for September 2026 (FRED series PAYEMS, diff). Later revisions are ignored.

research:
I was able to use pre-September-11 sources only through search snippets. The BLS, CNBC, UPI and Yahoo pages all refused the connection when I tried to fetch them directly.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the first published September 2026 change in BLS total nonfarm payrolls (CES, seasonally adjusted, in thousands). That number matches FRED PAYEMS month-over-month. Release date: Fri 2026-10-02, 8:30 ET. [financecalendar](https://www.financecalendar.com/event/us-employment-situation-non-farm-payrolls-september-2026/)
- 2026-09-04: The latest release, for August 2026 (USDL-26-1435), showed +162K and unemployment at 4.1%. [BLS archive](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_09042026.htm), [BLS TED](https://www.bls.gov/opub/ted/2026/payroll-employment-rose-162000-in-august-2026.htm)
- **Units warning:** the code baseline is in percent change. Total employment is roughly 159-160M (my approximation), so the baseline median of about 0.0985% works out to about +155K. The p5 to p95 range of -0.09% to +0.29% is roughly -145K to +460K. That distribution includes 2005-2024, when trend growth was much higher than in 2026, so it is probably biased upward.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The September data will not be published until 2026-10-02.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-10: First Trust says the preliminary benchmark revision (year to March 2026) was -79K total and -178K private, the smallest since 2021. [First Trust](https://www.ftportfolios.com/Commentary/EconomicResearch/2026/9/10/bls-payroll-revisions-fall-back-in-line-down-just-79,000)
- 2026-09-04, August report details:
  - +162K against a Dow Jones consensus of 53K and a FactSet consensus of 65K. It was the strongest month since March.
  - July was revised from -23K to +21K and June from 20K to 31K, so the two revisions added 55K together.
  - Food services led the gains and the information sector lost jobs.
  - Economists warned that August is often revised for seasonal reasons, and that the underlying 2026 trend is about 80K a month. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/04/jobs-report-august-2026.html), [NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/economy/august-jobs-report-trump-inflation-rcna595974), [PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/economy/hiring-burst-of-162000-jobs-in-august-puts-the-focus-squarely-back-on-inflation-in-the-u-s)
- 2026-09-02: ADP private payrolls for August were +38K (consensus about 47K), the weakest since January. July was revised to 46K. [ADP](https://mediacenter.adp.com/2026-09-02-ADP-National-Employment-Report-Private-Sector-Employment-Increased-by-38,000-Jobs-in-August)
- Late Aug 2026: ADP's weekly NER Pulse was rising from a low of about 8K a week (four weeks ending July 25). [investinglive](https://investinglive.com/news/adp-weekly-ner-pulse-16-500-vs-19-750-last-week)
- Aug-Sep 2026:
  - Fed Chair Warsh said at Jackson Hole that there is "work to do" on inflation.
  - Before the September 15-16 FOMC meeting, a 25bp hike was widely expected.
  - The labor market is described as stable. [Kiplinger](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/live/fed-meeting-updates-and-commentary-september-2026)

## 4. Base rates
- First prints in 2026: March about 178K, April about 115K, May about 172K, June 57K, July -23K, August 162K. That averages about 110K, with a range of -23K to 178K. [First Trust June](https://www.ftportfolios.com/Commentary/EconomicResearch/2026/7/2/nonfarm-payrolls-rose-57,000-in-june), [FactSet](https://insight.factset.com/total-nonfarm-payrolls-for-april-2026-are-projected-to-rise-by-65000)
- Recent first prints swing about 60-100K from month to month. In 2026, the miss against consensus has often been around ±100K (August beat by about 100K; July missed).
- A month after a big upside surprise is often weaker, but this is a loose pattern. The August report had economists citing trend growth of about 80K a month.

## 5. Other forecasts
- An undated preview found in search put the September consensus at about 90K. One forecasting-model page showed +157K. I could not confirm their dates, so treat them with caution. [therighttrader](https://therighttrader.com/economic-calendar/nonfarm-payrolls), [fedratecalc](https://fedratecalc.com/nonfarm-payrolls-release-date/)
- Kalshi KXPAYROLLS-26SEP: snapshots from May to July 2026 showed "above 0" at about 83¢ and "above 125K" at about 22-41¢ (the snapshots conflict). I found no current price as of 2026-09-11. [simplefunctions T125000](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/will-above-125000-jobs-be-added-in-september-2026-kalshi-kxpayrolls-26sep-t125000), [T0](https://simplefunctions.dev/api/agent/inspect/KXPAYROLLS-26SEP-T0)
- Manifold has a market on the September 2026 NFP; I did not get its price. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/CalibratedGhosts/will-september-2026-us-nonfarm-payr)
- I could not find a formal Bloomberg or Reuters consensus dated on or before 2026-09-11. It normally comes out in the week before the release.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Weekly jobless claims every Thursday. The claims for the reference week (the week containing September 12) come out around September 17.
- ADP NER Pulse weekly updates every Tuesday.
- FOMC decision on September 16. A hike could affect sentiment, but not September hiring itself.
- Late September: Conference Board labor differential.
- About September 30: ADP September monthly report.
- About October 1: ISM manufacturing employment index.
- Risk of a government shutdown at the October 1 fiscal-year start: I found no reporting on this. A shutdown could delay the October 2 release, as happened in 2025.
- 2026-10-02: BLS releases the September Employment Situation, which resolves the question.
